**`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`:** Yes, the page describes it:

> `Forbid`: The CronJob does not allow concurrent runs; if it is time for a new Job run and the previous Job run hasn't finished yet, the CronJob skips the new Job run. The other options are `Allow` (the default) and `Replace`, which replaces the running Job with a new one. The page also notes that this policy applies only to Jobs created by the same CronJob.
